subject: Post-call: KMS/CMK options & questionnaire for MediWise PoC
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Simone Durand <simone.durand@mediwise.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — KMS options for MediWise PoC

Thanks again for your time today, Simone — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Summary of ask (as I understood it):
- You want the PoC to exercise customer-managed key options (bring-your-own-key), demonstrate encryption at-rest/in-transit controls, and validate audit/log retention for HIPAA-covered workloads.
- Your security team will send a short vendor questionnaire we should complete.

What Redwood can do right away:
- We support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (CMKs). For CMKs we offer cross-account AWS KMS grants, GCP CMEK support, and an option to import key material to an HSM-backed path for stronger key control.
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ with mTLS available for private deployments; at-rest: AES-256 with per-customer key separation and optional HSM backing.
- Audit logs: token-level and request-level auditing with configurable retention; we can emit logs to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/Stackdriver).

Attachments: redwood-kms-overview.pdf (high-level), redwood-poa-kms-options.pdf (PoC approach)

Next steps I propose:
1) Please share the vendor questionnaire (or confirm you want us to start with our standard security packet).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) with your security/infra folks — availability Wed/Thu next week?
3) If CMKs are firm requirement, let us know whether you prefer keys in your cloud account (cross-account grant) or an imported HSM key managed by you.

If that aligns, I’ll drop a calendar invite and we can have Dev join for the technical detail.

— Jordan

Thanks, Jordan — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from our side and the security team: 

1) SOC 2: Are you currently SOC 2 Type II certified? If not, when is the audit scheduled and what scope will it cover?
2) HIPAA: Do you have a BAA in place and do you currently handle PHI in any hosted customers?
3) CMK options:
   - Can keys live in our AWS account (we prefer cross-account grants if possible)?
   - Do you support importable key material into an HSM (FIPS 140-2) so keys never leave our control?
4) Key rotation and lifecycle: how do you handle rotation, and can we enforce our rotation cadence?
5) Audit/logs: retention defaults and ability to forward to our SIEM (we use Splunk).
6) Questionnaire: I’ll attach our short vendor security questionnaire (a CSV). Please fill and return; security@mediwise.com will review.

Also: for the PoC we expect ~100 TPS bursts on inference at peak and about 1TB model cache per region. Happy to share more profile data if needed.

Could you reply with short answers and any links to documentation? If possible, include someone from your infra/crypto team on the next call.

— Simone

Appreciate the detailed questions — below are concise answers and links; happy to expand on any item on the technical call.

1) SOC 2: We are currently in the middle of a Type II attestation covering our hosted inference and control plane; fieldwork is scheduled for Nov 2026 with a target report date of Q1 2027. In the interim we provide our controls matrix and interim evidence. Link: https://redwood.com/security/soc2 (controls matrix and expected timeline).
2) HIPAA/BAA: We have a standard BAA template and several customers operate under HIPAA with us in Dedicated/Private modes. For Hosted customers we offer contractual safeguards and can discuss scoping for PoC. I’ll connect you with our legal CS lead if you want draft language.
3) CMK options:
   - Cross-account AWS KMS: supported. We implement least-privilege grants and can set up a role/grant that allows Redwood to use CMKs in your account without Redwood holding the key material.
   - Importable HSM-backed keys: supported for Dedicated/Private deployments; for hosted we offer an HSM-backed key path where key material can be kept in a customer-managed HSM in certain cases (requires additional onboarding & controls).
   - GCP CMEK: supported for GCP-hosted workloads.
4) Rotation: We support both provider-managed automatic rotation and customer-driven rotation. If you rotate keys in your account we honor the new key as long as grants/roles are updated; we can also coordinate rotation windows.
5) Audit/logs: Default retention is 90 days in the platform UI; we can stream audit events to your Splunk/SIEM with configurable retention buckets (30/90/365 days). We can also provide token-level and per-request metadata for compliance reviews.

Attachments I’m returning: mediwise-security-questionnaire.csv (filled), redwood-kms-overview.pdf (again), redwood-poa-kms-options.pdf (PoC plan).

Proposed next steps:
- Can we lock a technical deep-dive for Wed 10/21 at 11:00am PT? Dev will present the cross-account grant flow and options for HSM import.
- Please confirm whether you prefer keys in your account or an imported HSM-backed approach for the PoC.

Link to the folders with evidence & docs: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/mediwise/kms-poa

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Simone — quick technical addendum from our side before the call: 

- Cross-account AWS KMS flow we recommend: create a CMK in your account, create a grant allowing Redwood's service principal to Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey. We then mount the key via a secure grant role. This avoids key material ever leaving your account.
- HSM import: We support importing key material (RSA/AES) into an HSM-backed path for Dedicated/Private. For hosted with strict BYOK/HSM needs we can evaluate an EKM-like integration or a partner HSM gateway; this requires additional security review.
- Rotation handling: We recommend a monthly or quarterly rotation for CMKs at PoC; for production you can set your cadence. We can coordinate automated rekeying windows to avoid cache misses.
- Audit & key usage telemetry: we emit per-request key-id and operation; we can add your SIEM's ingestion endpoint during PoC to validate.
- PoC plan (high level):
   1) Baseline: run 48-hour traffic replay to reproduce your 100 TPS bursts using a representative prompt set.
   2) CMK validation: configure a cross-account CMK and run end-to-end encryption tests.
   3) HSM validation (if chosen): import sample key material to HSM-backed path and validate signing/decrypt flows.
   4) SIEM integration: stream logs to your Splunk instance and validate alerting/retention.

What we need from you before the deep-dive:
- Cloud account owner contact for cross-account set-up
- A short sample workload payloads and target RPS (you mentioned 100 TPS bursts)
- Any restrictive network/IP allowlists we need to configure

Happy to walk through the architecture on Wed — I’ll bring a diagram and the exact IAM/grant steps.

— Dev Patel
